newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares end mixed as locals dominate.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares end mixed as locals dominate.

text.p: The Lima Stock Exchange closed mixed Thursday as local investors dominated in trade marked by by both selective profit-taking and bargain-buying among the leaders, brokers said.
They predicted gains on Friday, although the market was expected to remain quiet as investors wait for corporate and macroeconomic results.
On Friday, the General Index rose 0.34 percent to 1,556.73 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index dipped 0.11 percent to 2,104.98.
Total market volume was a low 22.6 million soles ($8.8 million) on 1,196 trades as overall 29 stocks were flat, 25 fell and 23 rose.
"Today the local investors, with the news of the merger of the Backus group, traded strongly in the breweries, both to buy and to take profits," said Alberto Giha, of 4G brokerage.
Shareholders of the four breweries in Peru's Backus group will meet October 25 to decide on a possible merger plan.

The proposed new company, Cervecerias Peruanas Backus y Johnston, would include local blue-chips Cerveceria Backus y Johnston and Compania Nacional de Cerveza (CNC), and the smaller breweries Sociedad Cervecera de Trujillo S.A. and Cerveceria del Norte.
CNC fell overall by 3.68 percent to 1.57 soles on 2.2 million shares, while Backus y Johnston lost 1.11 percent to 2.67 soles on 430,864.

"We didn't see anything extraordinary in the market today. It was virtually stable. The leader, Telefonica del Peru, has been quiet now for various sessions," said Arien Lahura, of Interlima brokerage.

"With Telefonica, we are seeing that foreign investors prefer to trade it from New York rather than here because there is not an important margin of profit in the prices between both markets," he added.
Telefonica edged up 0.18 percent to 5.68 soles on 3.8 million shares, or 17 percent of total market volume.
